Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

appreciate verb

value, think highly of

also value (a person, a friendship), think highly of, prize, set great store by

classical

Cic. Att. 10.1.1: per enim magnī aestimō tibi firmitūdinem animī nostrī et factum nostrum probārī

magnī aestimāre

phrase: aestimō, aestimāre, aestimāvī, aestimātum with the genitive of value (magnī, plūris, plūrimī, parvī)

value highly, set great store by

The genitive says how highly: magnī, plūris (more), plūrimī (most), parvī (little). Aestimāre alone is to estimate, to value at a price (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • magnī facere — think highly of, value

    phrase: faciō with the genitive of value · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 15.14.2: quem jam diū plūrimī faciō; Cic. Fam. 3.4.2: duo enim duārum aetātum plūrimī faciō

    Common of people: aliquem plūrimī facere, to think the world of someone.

Examples

  • per enim magnī aestimō tibi firmitūdinem animī nostrī et factum nostrum probārī

    for I value it very highly that you approve of my firmness and of what I didCic. Att. 10.1.1

  • prīmum ut tē, quem jam diū plūrimī faciō, tantō intervallō vidērem

    first, to see you, whom I have long thought so highly of, after so longCic. Fam. 15.14.2

See also appreciate, value, respect, praise.

SourcesLewis & Short: aestimo · Lewis & Short: facio
